react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct network analysis) converge on two tightly linked one-carbon and phospholipid metabolism modules as the dominant biological signal. The clear cross-paradigm winner is Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / KEGG:hsa00260 / MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism), ranked first in RaMP ORA (FDR = 3.1×10⁻¹⁶, fold enrichment 663.7, 7 of 57 pathway members hit) and first in mummichog (p = 0.024, 8 of 8 compounds hit). Key driver metabolites are O-phospho-L-serine (phosphoserine, KEGG:C01005), choline (C00114), sarcosine (C00213), S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM, C00019), adenosine 5'-monophosphate (C00020), and (R)-lipoic acid (C16241), all resolved to canonical ChEBI IDs without structural conflict. The second coherent hit is Glycerophospholipid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00564, mummichog rank 2, p = 0.046), which shares choline and phosphocholine (C00588) as the driver pair, consistent with phospholipid head-group remodelling. Methionine and cysteine metabolism (RA MP/WP:WP2525 trans-sulfuration branch; mummichog rank 7) is supported by SAM and L-cystathionine (C02291). Biocytin (C05552) independently hits Vitamin H (biotin) metabolism (mummichog rank 6), while uridine 5'-monophosphate (C00105) contributes to Pyrimidine metabolism. Uridine 5'-monophosphate also appears in the N-Glycan biosynthesis pathway. The convergent biological story is a coordinated perturbation of one-carbon folate/trans-sulfuration networks and phospholipid membrane metabolism, consistent with a treatment that simultaneously affects methyl-donor flux (SAM, cystathionine), serine/glycine biosynthesis (phosphoserine, sarcosine), and choline-dependent phosphatidylcholine synthesis, with secondary hits to biotin handling and pyrimidine availability.

RaMP reports choline, O-phospho-L-serine, sarcosine, adenosine 5'-monophosphate, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, (R)-lipoic acid, and L-cystathionine as pathway members; mummichog independently recovers the same four core amino-acid intermediates (choline, phosphoserine, sarcosine, AMP) from mass-network inference alone. MetaboAnalystR confirms S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-cystathionine, and O-phospho-L-serine as members of the closely coupled Cysteine and methionine metabolism pathway (p 0.0009), reflecting the trans-sulfuration bridge between one-carbon folate cycling and hydrogen sulfide generation. Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MetaboAnalystR p 0.02; mummichog p 0.039) provides a secondary signal through the choline–phosphorylcholine pair, consistent with perturbation of phospholipid head-group availability. The driver set (phosphoserine, sarcosine, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-cystathionine) implicates coordinated disturbance of folate one-carbon interconversion and the CBS/ cystathionine beta-synthase trans-sulfuration hub.
